name: stale-ltads-state
question: Is ltads/arc-state.json inconsistent with the active-sessions.json registry (topmost arc ACTIVE/PAUSED but registry says closed/expired/missing/PID-dead)?
cost_provenance: measured 2026-06-12 on the ULDF framework repo under Git Bash (win32; slowest supported environment) -- pessimistic-honest per ORACLE-COST-01; under-declaration causes timeout kills

details.current_session_status: string|null (ACTIVE | PAUSED | CONCLUDED; topmost arc status)
details.registry_pid_alive: boolean|null (true/false when status=active and PID is non-null; null otherwise)

schema.briefing: string (empty when stale=false; one-liner suitable for ORACLE BRIEFING when stale=true)

fallback: Read ltads/arc-state.json (schema: templates/ARC_STATE_SCHEMA.md). The topmost arc is arcs[0]; its status field is the arc state. The registry-correlation id is the MOST-RECENT checkpoints[].by of the topmost arc (NOT the arc id, which is never a registry key). Read .claude/collaboration/active-sessions.json and find the entry whose .id == that sessionId. If the topmost arc status is ACTIVE/PAUSED but that entry is in closed[] / absent / its PID is not alive, that's a stale-state inconsistency. No checkpoints -> treat as consistent (stale:false). Legacy prose-only projects (no arc-state.json) -> consistent; the ltads-state oracle's legacy verdict surfaces the migration (ARC-11).

provenance.note: Third leg of CSI Phase 1.6's three-leg session-end cleanup defense. CSI-12 (SessionEnd hook) is proactive; CSI-13 (GC coupling) is reactive at next-session-start; CSI-14 is reflective -- it surfaces inconsistencies that slipped through both. Briefing-line emission gracefully absent when state is consistent. v1.1.0 (2026-07-22): re-anchored on ltads/arc-state.json via the ARC-02 lib (DEC-199); output schema unchanged.
